failed_decisions.description: Failed moves still asking for attention, as `/status` counts them.

move_files.description: Move the files on disk with each title. A key needs to be allowed to.

ApplyReport.description: Outcome of an apply or revert run.

moving.description:

waiting. Their decisions are `requested`, and the next sync confirms or
fails each.

oneOf.description:
Why the run ended before its last move, `null` when it ran through.
What was not attempted is still pending, or still applied for a revert.

superseded.description:
Selected proposals a newer simulation replaced with a different move,
not applied. One replaced by the same move is applied through it.

encrypted.description:
Sealed with the backup passphrase: a restore asks for it, and
`age -d` opens it without Routarr.

retention_count.description: How many are kept before the oldest is pruned.

BatchApplyReport.description: Outcome of applying a whole simulation, slice by slice.

batches_run.description: Slices actually attempted, fewer than planned when one of them failed.

candidates.description: Everything the simulation proposed and that was still applicable.

moving.description:
Moves of files the Arr was still making when the run stopped waiting,
as in `ApplyReport`.

oneOf.description: Why the run was stopped, `null` when it was not.

stopped_early.description:
True when the Arr refused a slice whole, one could not be read once
others had moved titles, or the run was stopped, and the remaining
ones were abandoned.

superseded.description:
Proposals of the simulation a newer one replaced with a different
move, not applied.

instance_names.description:
The instances the rule is limited to, by name. Absent for every
instance. A rule naming none this installation has is not imported.

BundledRule.description:
A rule as a bundle carries it, its instance scope by name: an id means
nothing on another installation, and a scope dropped would let the rule
route every instance.

CapacityForecast.description: One destination folder, and the weight of what this plan sends to it.

incoming_bytes.description:
Bytes arriving from a *different* filesystem, which is the only traffic
that consumes space (see `fits`).

same_filesystem_bytes.description:
Bytes arriving from a folder that reports the same free space, and so
almost certainly sits on the same filesystem. A move there is a rename
and costs nothing.

Category.description: A user-defined category for media classification.

CategoryWithUsage.description: A category with the counts that make it safe (or unsafe) to delete.

oneOf.description:
Media added to the Arr instance within the last N days, N times 24

value.description:
Media added to the Arr instance within the last N days, N times 24
hours, so a rule can target new additions without touching the
existing library. An Arr clock less than a day ahead reads as just
added. At least 1.

oneOf.description: Monitoring flag in Radarr/Sonarr.

value.description: Monitoring flag in Radarr/Sonarr.

oneOf.description: Whether any source, the Arr included, supplied a field a condition reads.

value.description: Whether any source, the Arr included, supplied a field a condition reads.

ConditionCatalog.description: The conditions a rule may use, and how a rule combines them.

ConditionOutcome.description: One condition of a rule, held against a title.

expected.description: What the condition asked for, in the interface language.

key.description: Translation key describing what the rule asked for.

observed.description: What the media actually carried, verbatim.

source.description:
Which metadata source supplied `observed`, absent for a condition the
Arr answers directly.

ConditionSpec.description: One condition a rule may use.

available.description:
Whether an enabled source answers that field. A condition no source
answers matches nothing.

counterpart.description: The condition asking the same question the other way, empty when none.

label.description: The caption, in the interface language.

label_key.description: The dictionary key of the caption.

media_types.description: `movie`, `series` or both: where it can ever match.

metadata_field.description: The metadata field it reads, if any.

needs_metadata.description: Whether it reads metadata a source supplies.

quantifier.description: `any` or `all` for a condition asked both ways, empty otherwise.

suggestions.description:
The `/media/facets` axis its values are drawn from, empty where they
are not a closed set.

type.description: The `type` a condition is written with.

Confirmed.description:
The guardrails the caller has looked at and accepts: `capacity`,
`threshold`, `batch` or `unreachable`.

CreateOverrideRequest.description: A title to pin, and the category to pin it to.

media_id.description: The title's id in Routarr, as `/media` lists it.

target_category.description: The name of an existing category.

CreateRuleRequest.description:
A rule as written: what `POST /rules`, `PUT /rules/{id}`, `/rules/validate`
and `/rules/preview` take.

priority.description:
Lower is tried first. Equal priorities go by name, then by id. Left
out, a new rule goes after every other, and an edited one keeps its
place.

Decision.description: A routing decision computed by the rule engine.

actor.description:
What set the decision off: `manual`, `schedule`, `webhook`, `api`, or
`auto` for the simulation the automation runs after a sync.

confidence.description: 0.0 to 1.0, how many independent signals backed the winning rule.

reverted_at.description: Set when the move was rolled back through `POST /decisions/revert`.

revertible.description:
Whether a revert may undo this move now: only the latest standing move
of a title is, while the title is still where it put it and the folder
it came from is still one of its instance's root folders.

simulation_id.description: Groups every decision produced by the same simulation run.

subject.description:
Who asked: an application's name, or the person a sign-in mode names.
Null when nobody asked (the scheduler or a webhook), and under a mode
that names nobody. An application key reads its own name and null for
anyone else.

superseded.description:
True once this proposal was retired: by a newer simulation, an override
set or removed, a revalidation that found it stale, or the removal of
its media or its instance.

DeclareRootFolder.description: Request to declare a destination the Arr does not report.

path.description: As stored: closed by the separator the Arr writes.

verified.description:
The Arr reported the folder when it was declared. Unverified, it is
tried at the next sync.

ErrorResponse.description: The envelope every refusal and failure answers.

answerable.description: Beside `confirm`: whether this caller may send the name back.

confirm.description:
The guardrail that asks, for `confirmation_required`. Sending it back
in `confirm` accepts that question and no other.

error.description:
A stable code: `bad_request`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `not_found`,
`conflict`, `confirmation_required`, `too_many_requests`, `busy`,
`reauthentication_required`, `passphrase_required`, `external_api_error`,
or an internal kind.

includes.description:
Beside `confirm`: the other guardrails the question states, sent back
in `confirm` with it to accept the question whole.

message.description:
A sentence for a person, in the interface language. Never part of the
contract.

instance_enabled.description:
False when the title's instance is switched off: no run reads it, and
the move shown is only what the rules would do.

rule_traces.description: Per-condition outcome for every rule that was considered.

Facet.description: One value a condition can hold, and how many items carry it.

group.description:
What the value means, where several values mean the same thing: codes
of several countries rate a film alike, and a rule wants every one.

label.description:
What to show instead of `value`, where the two differ. Absent for a
genre, which is its own label.

value.description:
What a rule stores and the engine compares. Never the displayed text: a
language is matched on `ja`, however it is shown.

create_missing_categories.description: Create any missing category referenced by the bundle.

replace.description: Delete every existing rule first instead of appending.

api_key_encrypted.description: Whether the stored API key is encrypted at rest.

api_key_masked.description: The Arr's key, masked. Empty for an application key.

last_sync_at.description: When a sync last *succeeded*. Null while none ever has.

last_sync_attempt_at.description:
When one was last attempted, successful or not: the figure that says
whether the scheduler is running at all.

webhook_path.description:
The same without the token, which goes in `X-Routarr-Token`: Radarr
5.16 and Sonarr 4.0.11 send custom headers. `null` for an application
key.

webhook_token.description: The token for `X-Routarr-Token`. `null` for an application key.

webhook_url.description:
Relative URL to register in Radarr/Sonarr's webhook connection, the
token in it, for an Arr that sends no custom header. `null` for an
application key: its token lets anyone post events as the Arr.

detail.description: What the task did, in the interface language.

result.description:
What a finished task answered: the report the same call gives when the
caller waits, an `ApplyReport`, a `BatchApplyReport` or a `SyncReport`,
or for a simulation its `SimulationResult`. A stored simulation's comes
without `decisions`, which `GET /decisions?simulation_id=` lists, and a
preview's keeps the ones it returned. An apply or a revert that failed
keeps the report of what it attempted. Null while the task runs, when
any other task failed, for a kind no call starts, and in the list
unless it asks for it.

status.description:
`running`, `success`, `failed`, or `cancelled` for an apply or a
revert somebody stopped.

subject.description:
Who asked: an application's name, or the person a sign-in mode names.
An application key reads its own name and null for anyone else.

trigger.description:
What set the task off: `manual`, `schedule`, `webhook`, `api`, or `auto`
for what the automation runs after a sync.

LibraryFacets.description:
What the library holds on each axis a condition reads, each value with
how many titles carry it: what a rule can be written against.

origin_countries.description:
The countries the library's titles come from, counted like the
languages.

statuses.description: The statuses the Arrs give the titles, as they write them.

vocabularies.description:
Every language and country a rule may name, whether the library holds
it or not: their codes are a closed vocabulary.

without_metadata.description:
Titles no enabled source describes, which no condition reading
metadata can match.

actor.description:
What set the write off: `manual`, `schedule`, `webhook`, `api` for an
application key, or `auto` for a move the automation applied.

subject.description:
Who asked, when the mode vouched for a name, or the application key's
name. An application key reads its own name here and `null` for anyone
else's.

Mapped.description: The category a folder now leads to.

category.description: `null` once the folder leads to no category.

MappingConflict.description: A mapping problem the user should resolve.

MatchMode.description: How the conditions of a rule combine.

subject.description:
An application's name, the signed-in person, `apikey` for the owner's
key, or `anonymous` where the mode asks for nothing.

genres.description: The genres Radarr or Sonarr reports, as a JSON array in a string.

original_language.description: ISO 639-1, normalised from the Arr's language *name* at sync time.

season_count.description: Seasons excluding specials, null for movies.

series_type.description:
Sonarr's own classification (`standard`, `anime` or `daily`), null for
movies.

tags.description: The Arr's tag labels, as a JSON array in a string.

computed_category.description:
The category the last stored run sends the title to, whether it moves

certification_scale.description:
The system the certification belongs to: an ISO 3166-1 country code,
or `MAL` for MyAnimeList's. Absent when the source did not say.

field_sources.description: Field name -> the source that supplied it. Only populated fields appear.

sources.description: Sources that supplied at least one field, highest priority first.

genre_list.description: The genres the Arr reports: `genres` holds the same as a JSON string.

tag_list.description: The Arr's tag labels: `tags` holds the same as a JSON string.

A media row as the API shows one, its lists read out of the JSON strings
the row keeps them in.

media_missing_metadata.description: Items no source describes at all.

providers.description: Every source in the user's order, whether or not it can answer.

configured.description: A source that needs a key and has one, or that needs none.

connected.description:
Probed only for a fetched, configured source. Null for the Arr, whose
instances are probed on their own.

NewRuleTest.description: What a caller supplies to pin a case.

expected_category.description: Defaults to what the engine decides for that item today.

The library item to snapshot. Resolved once, here, and never referenced

allowed_mentions.description:

content.description: The message again, where Discord reads it.

Ids and counts for a program: the instance, the simulation, how many

`instance_recovered`, `auto_apply_failed`, `sync_failed`,

message.description: A sentence in English for a person.

type.description:
The outcome as Apprise reads it: `failure`, `warning`, `success` or
`info`.

OverrideEntry.description:
An exception: a title pinned to a category by hand, which outranks every

computed_category.description:
The category the last stored run sends the title to, whether it moves
or already sits there. Null until a run has evaluated it.

PinRequest.description: The category to pin a title to, and why.

target_category.description: The name of an existing category.

PinnedCategory.description: The category an exception pins a title to, and why.

Placement.description:
What `GET /route` answers: one placement per instance that holds or knows
the title, and what went wrong on the others.

errors.description: An instance that could not be asked, which stops none of the others.

PlacementAnswer.description: Where one instance would put the title.

action.description:
`add` for a title the Arr does not hold yet, else `move` or `none`.
`skip` when the category has no folder on this instance.

category.description: The category the rules or an exception choose, or the default one.

media_id.description: The title's id in Routarr, for a title the library holds.

oneOf.description: The folder mapped to that category on this instance, null when none is.

rule.description: The winning rule's name, null when none matched or an exception decided.

source.description:
`library` when Routarr holds the title for this instance, `lookup`
when only the Arr knows it.

unanswered_fields.description:
The metadata fields a rule tried up to the winner reads that no source
answered: `genres`, `keywords`, `original_language`, `origin_countries`
or `certification`. A source answering one may change the placement.

PlacementFolder.description: A destination, and whether the Arr reports it or only Routarr declares it.

origin.description:
`arr` for a root folder the Arr reports, `declared` for one only
Routarr knows, which the Arr may refuse until it is added there.

status.description: Always `ok`: an answer at all is the news.

rule.description:
The rule being edited. When `rule_id` is set it replaces that rule,
otherwise it is appended to the current set.

after.description: What the library looks like with the candidate rule applied.

changed.description: Media whose target category changes because of this rule.

PreviewSummary.description: What one rule set decides over the library, counted.

configured.description: Whether it can answer today: it needs no key, or its key is set.

display_name.description: A proper noun, never translated, like "Radarr" and "Sonarr".

fetched.description: False for a source whose data arrives with the library sync.

fields.description: The fields it can supply, so the interface can say what enabling it buys.

key_env.description:
The environment variable its credential is read from, so the interface
can name it instead of saying "a key is missing".

order.description: Enabled sources, highest priority first. Everything not listed is off.

RenameCategoryRequest.description: Request body for renaming a category.

rule_ids.description: Ordered list of rule IDs, from highest priority (index 0) to lowest.

Reordered.description: How many rules a reorder numbered.

RevertDecisionsRequest.description: Request to roll a previously applied decision back to its original folder.

confirm.description: The guardrails the caller has looked at, by name, as for an apply.

decision_ids.description: The applied decisions to move back.

move_files.description: Move the files on disk with each title. A key needs to be allowed to.

RootFolder.description: A root folder synchronized from an Arr instance.

arr_id.description: The folder's id in the Arr, `null` for a folder Routarr declares.

last_accessible_at.description:
When the folder last answered, as opposed to when it was last seen in a
pass. `null` for one that has never answered.

origin.description:
`arr` for a folder the instance reports, `declared` for one typed into
Routarr. Only the second may be deleted here.

RootFolderWithInstance.description: Root folder with instance info for display.

Rule.description: A routing rule that maps conditions to a target category.

exclusions.description: Conditions that disqualify the rule even when `conditions` match.

priority.description: Lower is tried first. Equal priorities go by name, then by id.

categories.description: Categories referenced by the rules, so an import can recreate them.

exported_at.description: When it was written, in RFC 3339.

version.description:
The format, which this build writes as 2. A version 1 bundle names no
instance a rule is limited to, and its rules without instance ids are
imported switched off.

RuleHealth.description: One rule, and what the library says about it.

ambiguous_with.description:
Another rule with the same priority and the same name, so that which
of the two wins is no decision anybody made.

duplicate_of.description:
Another rule with the same conditions and the same target. One of the
two decides nothing whatever the priorities are.

matched_nothing.description:
It matched nothing at all. That is a different problem from being
shadowed, and usually a condition that is too narrow rather than a
priority that is too low. Never said of a disabled rule, which no run
reads.

shadowed.description: Items it matched and lost on priority.

shadowed_by.description: The rule that took the most of what this one matched, when it never won.

vetoed.description: Items it matched and had vetoed by one of its own exclusions.

adjusted.description:
Each rule imported otherwise than the bundle has it, with how: limited
to fewer instances, or switched off until its scope is checked.

replaced.description: The rules in place were removed first.

skipped.description: Each rule left out, with why.

RuleTest.description: A stored case: inputs, and the category they are required to produce.

RuleTestResult.description: What one case did on this run.

actual_category.description: What the engine says today. `null` when the stored fixture fails to parse.

error.description: Set when the fixture itself is the problem rather than the rules.

matched_rule.description: The rule that won, so a failure names what took the decision.

conditions.description: Every condition, with its wording already resolved for this language.

RuleVerdict.description: What the server makes of a draft rule.

valid.description: False when an issue is an error: the rule would be refused.

max_returned.description: Cap the payload size. The counters always reflect the full library.

persist.description: Store the decisions so they can be applied. `false` is a pure preview.

persist_unchanged.description: Also keep decisions for media already in the right place.

capacity.description:
What the plan would put on each destination, and whether it fits.

Only destinations that receive something appear, and only when the Arr
reported a free-space figure for them.

excluded_by_rule.description:
How often a rule matched a title and one of its own exclusions set it
aside, over every title, rules below the winner included.

returned.description: How many decisions are included in `decisions` after truncation.

skipped_unmapped.description: Matched a category with no root folder mapped on that instance.

StatusResponse.description: Counts and warnings, read from the database without probing anything.

dry_run.description: Whether the global dry run holds, in which case nothing is moved.

failed_decisions.description:
Failed moves still asking for attention: each its title's latest
decision, which no later run has settled.

warnings.description: Configuration problems detectable without touching the network.

StopReason.description: Why a run that moves titles ended before its last move.

info.description:
The part of Routarr's API another application may rely on: a script, n8n, Home Assistant or a dashboard.

Authenticate with an application key, made on Routarr's Applications screen, sent as `X-Api-Key: rtr_...` or `Authorization: Bearer rtr_...`. Each operation names the scope it needs in `x-routarr-scope`. Every key reads, and `operate`, `write` and `configure` are granted each on its own. The owner's key reaches every operation.

A failure answers one envelope: `error`, a stable code, and `message`, a sentence in the interface language that is not part of the contract. A move that crosses a guardrail answers 409 `confirmation_required` with the guardrail's name in `confirm`, and in `includes` the other guardrails its question states. Send those names back in `confirm` to go ahead, or, when `answerable` is false, leave the question to a person.

A call that starts long work (a simulation, an apply, a revert, the sync of one instance) waits for it and answers its report. Sent with `Prefer: respond-async`, it answers 202 as soon as the task has started, with `Location` naming the task: `GET /jobs/{id}` follows it, and its `result` holds the report once it has finished. A guardrail's question and any refusal still answer at once.

The notification webhook set in Routarr's settings receives a `Notification` for each failure, and for the syncs that failed, the simulations and the moves that finished when asked to. A format set to Discord, ntfy, Gotify or Apprise, or recognised from a Discord or ntfy.sh address, writes the same events in that receiver's own shape instead, which this contract does not cover. With a signing secret every shape is signed as Standard Webhooks specifies: `webhook-id`, stable across retries, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature`, `v1,` and a base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body` under the secret's key, twice while a new secret replaces an old one. A delivery refused with 5xx or 429, or not answered, is tried again after 10 s, 60 s and 5 min.

An application key asks at most ten times a second past a burst of fifty, and takes a backup at most every ten minutes. Past either it is answered `429`, with `Retry-After` in seconds.

Nothing documented under `/api/v1` is removed or renamed, and no field changes type. New operations, new fields and new values of the open lists (`action`, `status`, `error`, `confirm`, the kinds of a condition) may appear in any release.
